_nota: Summary of INIFAP's 2026 Agricultural Technical Agenda, prepared from the text in data/inifap/extraido/zacatecas.json following pipeline/inifap/instrucciones_resumen.md. No pesticide brands or doses.
fuente: INIFAP. Agenda Técnica Agrícola de Zacatecas [Agricultural Technical Agenda of Zacatecas]. INIFAP, Mexico City, 2026.

fichas.region: Zacatecas Altiplano, 1,900 to 2,300 m a.s.l., temperate arid subtropical and warm semiarid climate. Soils 30 to 50 cm deep, sandy loam to clayey, with slope under 8 %; not suitable with electrical conductivity above 4 mmhos/cm.

siembra.texto: From September 15 to October 31. It can be planted until November, but yield and quality drop; earlier varieties tolerate later plantings.

fichas.densidad: Beds of 1.52 to 2.00 m with six rows and three drip tapes. With drip or sprinkler irrigation, about 600,000 plants/ha can be reached, but above 450,000 (less than 10 cm between plants) the bulbs come out smaller. Use bulbs of 35 mm or more as seed, and cloves of 8 mm or more.
fichas.fertilizacion: Do a soil analysis. For 20 t/ha with 333,000 plants/ha: 250 kg of N, 100 of P, 265 of K and 120 of Ca per ha. Apply 50-50-50-15 (N-P-K-Ca) before planting and the rest through the irrigation system every 10 days, according to crop uptake.
fichas.riego: Drip irrigation scheduled with the Class A evaporation pan and the crop coefficient (Kc): 0.4 in the vegetative stage (September to December), 0.6 in development (January to March) and 0.7 in bulbing (April to June).
fichas.malezas: Critical period: the first 35 days after planting, although it is best to keep the crop clean throughout the cycle so as not to hinder field work or harvest. If needed, make one cultivator pass in the alleys between beds.
fichas.cosecha: Harvest when the cloves are well formed and the bulb has 3 to 5 wrapper leaves; the false stem softens or the plants lodge (or the flower stalk is fully extended). Stop irrigation, loosen the soil, collect and bundle to dry. Store at 15-18 °C in a dry, ventilated place. Up to 28 t/ha can be obtained.
cuidados: Plant between September 15 and October 31; November plantings yield less.
Use healthy seed: bulbs of 35 mm or more and cloves of 8 mm or more, stored in ventilated boxes in a cool place.
Sample the soil before planting and do not bring soil, plants or equipment from plots with white rot or nematodes; do not repeat garlic or onion for at least 4 years where nematodes were present.
Keep the crop free of weeds, especially during the first 35 days.
Against thrips, ensure good spray coverage and rely on natural enemies (lacewings, ladybugs, minute pirate bug) and entomopathogenic fungi.
Cut the neck only when it is dry, avoid bruising and discard blue-green bulbs to prevent Penicillium rot in storage.
fichas.nota: Costs from Table 5: the total cost (296,727.20) matches the sum of the items and the gross income (381,531.60) matches 18 t × 21,196.20 $/t. The price is in $/t. Net income is not printed and was calculated as gross income − cost; the printed B/C (1.28) is truncated (the calculation gives 1.29). The yield in the table (18 t/ha) is lower than the potential in the text (28 t/ha).

fichas.region: Temperate arid and warm semiarid subtropics, up to 2,500 m a.s.l. Best in fields with 0 to 1 % slope, medium texture, soil deeper than 0.5 m and electrical conductivity below 4 mmhos/cm.

siembra.texto: Irrigated (FW cycle): December 15 to January 30. Rainfed (SS cycle): from the onset of the rains until July 31.

fichas.densidad: Irrigated: 75 to 100 kg/ha of seed in double-row furrows and 120 to 150 kg/ha broadcast or in contour corrugations. Rainfed: 80 kg/ha in double-row furrows with small basins (pileteo) and 130 kg/ha in corrugations with small basins or broadcast. Furrows of 76 cm with rows 20 cm apart; seed no deeper than 5 cm.
fichas.fertilizacion: Irrigated: 120-60-00, with 60-60-00 at planting and 60-00-00 at tillering (broadcast, before tillering so that machinery does not damage plants). Rainfed: 40-40-00 in high potential, 30-30-00 in medium and 20-20-00 in low, all at planting. A prior soil analysis is advisable.
fichas.riego: With severe water restriction: planting irrigation and irrigations at 45 and 75 days. With moderate availability: planting, 45, 75 and 100 days. Without restriction: up to five irrigations at 15, 35, 65, 85 and 105 days. Drip tape saves water and allows fertilizer to be applied through irrigation.
plagas: English grain aphid (Macrosiphum avenae / Sitobion avenae)
fichas.malezas: Plant into moist soil and harrow before planting to eliminate weeds; each cultivation pass removes those that emerge afterward. Broadleaf weeds are the most common; if they are a problem, control is done at tillering.
fichas.cosecha: At physiological maturity: golden head and hard grain that does not split when pressed with a fingernail. By hand, make bundles and thresh at 12 % moisture. Yield of up to 5 t/ha in high potential and 4 t/ha in medium.
cuidados: Plant on time: December 15 to January 30 under irrigation and before July 31 under rainfed conditions.
Use the recommended varieties according to the potential of the field; they are tolerant to diseases.
Watch for aphids during the two weeks after emergence: act at 3 to 5 aphids per plant in the first week and 15 per plant afterward.
As an alternative, use biodegradable detergent (4 g per liter) or release lacewings (1 egg per 2 aphids) after sampling.
Lay out furrows on contour lines and make small basins (pileteo) in rainfed fields to capture moisture and slow erosion.
Consider vertical tillage with chisels instead of disk plowing to conserve moisture and soil.

fichas.region: Temperate arid and warm semiarid subtropics, up to 2,500 m a.s.l. and 10 to 18 °C annual mean, slope under 4 %. Under rainfed conditions, potential depends on the July-to-September precipitation/evaporation index and on the soil being deeper than 0.5 m.

siembra.texto: From the onset of the rains until July 31. Vegetative cycle of about 100 days.

fichas.densidad: 80 kg/ha of seed in double-row furrows with small basins (pileteo) (76 cm furrows, rows 20 cm apart) and 130 to 150 kg/ha in corrugations with small basins or broadcast; cover the seed to 5 cm.
fichas.fertilizacion: 40-40-00 in high potential, 30-30-00 in medium and 20-20-00 in low, before or at planting. A prior soil analysis is advisable.
fichas.malezas: Harrow after the rains and before planting into moist soil; each cultivation pass removes the weeds that emerge. Broadleaf weeds are the most common; if they are a problem, control is done at tillering.
fichas.cosecha: At the milk stage of the grain (soft grain that releases a whitish liquid when pressed). By hand, form bundles and thresh when the forage is dehydrated. Expected yield of 12 t/ha of green matter in high potential and 7 t/ha in medium.
cuidados: Plant with the onset of the rains and no later than July 31.
Use rust-resistant varieties: Diamante R-31 and Turquesa are the most resistant.
Make small basins (pileteo) at the first cultivation where rainfall is low or there is erosion risk, and lay out furrows on contour lines.
Watch for aphids after emergence: act at 3 to 5 per plant in the first week and 15 per plant afterward; as an alternative, biodegradable detergent (4 g/L) or lacewing release.
Harvest at the milk stage of the grain to obtain good forage.
fichas.nota: Table 13: total cost (13,225.50) matches the sum of the items and gross income (10,818) matches 12 t of green matter × 901.50 $/t. Net income is not printed and was calculated (it comes out negative); the printed B/C of 0.81 is truncated (the calculation gives 0.82). The diseases text mentions rust-susceptible varieties (Guelatao, Tulancingo, Ópalo, Cuauhtémoc, Cevamex, Páramo and Chihuahua).

fichas.region: Rainfed SS cycle with mean temperature of 16 to 21 °C and 320 to 800 mm of rain from June to October (high potential with 380 to 800 mm), slope under 4 % and soil deeper than 0.5 m.

siembra.texto: At the onset of the rains, into moist soil; plantings after July 15 have a higher risk of frost damage.

fichas.densidad: 1.5 to 2.5 kg/ha of seed in furrows of 76 to 81 cm in single rows, at a depth of 2 to 3 cm.
fichas.fertilizacion: There is no economic optimum rate for rainfed conditions. In areas of medium and good potential (Río Grande, 400 to 600 mm per cycle), 100-50-30 responded well: half of the N and all of the P at planting and the rest of the N at the first cultivation. In Fresnillo and Zacatecas (less than 400 mm), 50-20-00 gave better results, applied at planting or with the N split between planting and the first cultivation.
enfermedades: Black spot or Alternaria blight of crucifers (Alternaria brassicae)
fichas.malezas: Critical period: the first 40 days after planting; after that, canola competes on its own. Make two cultivations: the first at 25 days (plants 6 to 15 cm tall) and the second with plants 30 to 40 cm tall (15 to 20 days later).
fichas.cosecha: When the pods are yellowish brown and the grain has 12 to 15 % moisture. Thresh preferably early in the morning or in the afternoon to avoid shattering; adjust the combine (plug holes, raise the reel, calibrate the concave). Potential yield of 2.0 to 3.0 t/ha.
cuidados: Prepare the field very well and leave it level: the seed is very small and is planted at 2 to 3 cm.
Plant at the onset of the rains, before July 15, to reduce the risk of frost.
Keep the crop clean for the first 40 days and eliminate wild crucifers (wild mustard) around it one week before planting.
Flea beetle: act at more than 3 insects per plant in the first weeks. Aphid: monitor with yellow traps and act when 20 % of stems are infested at the end of flowering; protect their natural enemies.
Use pheromone traps to detect imported cabbageworm early.
Against white rust and black spot: healthy seed, crop rotation and incorporation of crop residues.
fichas.nota: Table 16: total cost (22,948.75) matches the sum of the items and gross income (16,080) matches 2 t × 8,040 $/t; B/C of 0.70 is consistent. Net income is not printed and was calculated (it comes out negative). The agenda does not say who obtained Armada, Monty, IMC-104 and IMC-105; they were left under varieties because it could not be confirmed that they are commercial. Canola is no longer planted in the state; it is proposed as a crop conversion option.

fichas.region: Up to 2,500 m a.s.l., best with 0 to 1 % slope, medium texture, soil deeper than 0.5 m and electrical conductivity below 4 mmhos/cm.

siembra.texto: Irrigated (FW): Adabella and Esmeralda from December 15 to January 25; Esperanza and Armida from December 15 to January 15. Rainfed (SS): Adabella and Esmeralda from the onset of the rains until July 30.

fichas.densidad: Irrigated: Adabella and Esmeralda 75 kg/ha in double-row furrows and 150 broadcast or in corrugations; Esperanza and Armida 100 and 150 kg/ha. Rainfed: 80 kg/ha in double rows with small basins (pileteo) and 130 in corrugations or broadcast. Furrows of 76 cm with rows 20 cm apart; seed no deeper than 5 cm.
fichas.fertilizacion: Irrigated: the agenda gives 120-60-60 in two parts: 60-60-00 at planting and 60-00-00 at tillering (broadcast, before tillering). In sandy soils, split the N; in heavy soils, apply everything at planting. Rainfed: 40-40-00 in high potential, 30-30-00 in medium and 20-20-00 in low, at planting.
fichas.riego: With severe water restriction: planting irrigation and irrigations at 45 and 75 days. With moderate availability: 45, 75 and 100 days. Without restriction: five irrigations at 15, 35, 65, 85 and 105 days. Drip tape makes water use more efficient.
fichas.malezas: Plant into moist soil and harrow before planting. Broadleaf weeds are controlled at tillering; watch for wild oats between 25 and 30 days after planting. Do not make applications during grain filling.
fichas.cosecha: At physiological maturity: golden head and hard grain that does not split with a fingernail. By hand, bundles and threshing at 12 % moisture. Expected yield under irrigation of 6 t/ha in high potential and 4 t/ha in medium; under rainfed conditions, 3.5 to 4.0 t/ha in high and 2 to 3 t/ha in medium.
cuidados: Plant on time: mid-December to January under irrigation and before July 30 under rainfed conditions.
Use the recommended varieties, which are tolerant to diseases.
Watch for aphids in the early stages, especially Russian wheat aphid: management is justified at 4 aphids per seedling or 10 per tiller.
As an alternative, biodegradable detergent (4 g/L) or release lacewings (1 egg per 2 aphids).
Lay out furrows on contour lines and make small basins (pileteo) in rainfed fields.
Split the nitrogen in sandy soils.
fichas.nota: Tables 19 (irrigated) and 20 (rainfed), both with the variety Doña Josefa. Total costs match the sum of the items and gross incomes match yield × price ($/t). Net income calculated (not printed); the rainfed B/C is truncated (0.559). The irrigated rate says 120-60-60, but the two applications it describes add up to 120-60-00 and the cost table uses diammonium phosphate and ammonium sulfate with no potassium. The variety table (Table 18) came out split across the planting and varieties sections; the assignment of densities and dates was deduced from the order of the text.

fichas.region: Zacatecas Altiplano, 1,500 to 2,300 m a.s.l., 14 to 19 °C annual mean. Soils 30 to 50 cm deep, sandy loam to clayey, with slope under 8 %; not suitable with electrical conductivity above 4 mmhos/cm.

siembra.texto: Short photoperiod: seedbed from September to November and transplanting from December to March. Intermediate photoperiod: seedbed from December to February and transplanting from March to May. Seedlings are transplanted 70 to 90 days after sowing.

fichas.densidad: 333,000 plants/ha in beds of 1.52 to 2 m with six rows, 10 cm between plants and three drip tapes. Transplant when the bulb measures 3 to 7 mm and the plant 30 to 40 cm.
fichas.fertilizacion: Soil, water and plant analysis. In six-row beds: 200-100-100. Before transplanting, apply up to 40 % of the N and K and half of the P; the rest of the P through the drip tape in the first 50 days, and the N and K in 14 weekly applications (5 to 10 % per week).
fichas.riego: 350 to 550 mm per cycle. Shallow roots: light, frequent irrigations, with neither drought nor waterlogging. Abundant irrigation at transplanting; during vegetative growth every 2 to 4 days, when 25 % of the available water is depleted. The most critical stage is the start and filling of the bulb. Stop irrigation 15 to 25 days before harvest.
fichas.malezas: Keep the crop free of weeds for the first 50 to 60 days after transplanting.
fichas.cosecha: When new leaves stop emerging and the neck becomes limp: stop irrigation, lift the bulbs and remove roots and foliage. Expected yield of up to 130 t/ha with short-photoperiod hybrids and 115 t/ha with intermediate-photoperiod ones.
cuidados: Choose the material according to photoperiod and respect its seedbed and transplanting dates.
Give light, frequent irrigations, without lacking water during bulb filling, and stop 15 to 25 days before harvest.
Keep the crop clean for the first 50 to 60 days after transplanting.
Monitor leafminer adults and thrips; use natural enemies and entomopathogenic fungi as an alternative.
Sample the soil and do not bring soil, plants or equipment from plots with white rot; do not transplant for at least 5 years where pink root was present.
Against downy mildew: well-drained soils, furrows oriented toward the wind, avoid high density and sprinkler irrigation, and rotate for at least 3 years.
fichas.nota: Table 25: total cost (100,614.45) matches the sum of the items and gross income (479,624.40) matches 120 t × 3,996.87 $/t; B/C of 4.76 is consistent. Net income calculated (not printed). The agenda presents the cultivars as 'hybrids and varieties' without saying which is which or the company; they were placed under commercial because none is identified as public. The planting months are those of the seedbed; the cycle is left as null because transplanting runs from December to May. The cost table labels the fertilization as 250-100-265, which differs from the rate in the text (200-100-100).

fichas.region: Zacatecas Altiplano, 1,900 to 2,300 m a.s.l., temperate arid and warm semiarid subtropical climate with summer rains; 13 to 24 °C mean and more than 1,400 heat units from April to September. Soils 30 to 50 cm deep, slope under 8 %.
fichas.densidad: Mirasol, guajillo and puya: 39,693 plants/ha in 0.76 m furrows with 33 cm between clumps (gravity irrigation) or 43,290 plants/ha in 1.52 m beds with two rows and 30 cm between clumps (drip). Landrace puya and árbol: 52,400 plants/ha at 25 cm. Ancho, mulato and pasilla: 68,906 plants/ha at 19 cm in furrows, or 27,500 plants/ha in 1.80 m beds with 40 cm between clumps (drip). One plant per clump.
fichas.fertilizacion: Soil, water and plant analysis. With drip irrigation in mirasol chili: 200-75-100. The P in two parts of 37.5 kg: 20 days after transplanting and 40 days later. The N and K little by little through irrigation during the whole cycle, with a base of 15 to 20 % before transplanting.
fichas.riego: Drip daily or at least twice a week depending on soil texture. Drip tape buried at 20 cm saves 30 % of the water. Replace evapotranspiration (ETo = evaporation × 0.75) with Kc of 0.30-0.40 in growth (0 to 40 days), 0.60-0.75 in flowering and fruit set (40 to 125 days) and 0.40-0.50 at maturity (125 to 160 days).
fichas.malezas: Keep free of weeds for at least 12 weeks after transplanting with timely cultivations and hoeing; when machinery can no longer enter or when it rains, hand weeding.
fichas.cosecha: Mirasol, ancho, pasilla, mulato, puya and árbol are harvested dry; ancho can be harvested green with one picking at 130-140 days after transplanting. Dried chili is picked as it ripens (change from green to red or dark brown) from 150 days, up to five pickings in a month and a half. Expected yield of 3 to 4 t/ha in furrows and 3 to 5 t/ha in drip beds.
cuidados: Transplant between April 15 and May 5.
Level the field, drain excess water and avoid heavy irrigations to prevent chili wilt; incorporate organic matter and rotate away from solanaceous crops.
Weevil: act at 1 adult per 400 reproductive terminals and collect fallen fruit.
Monitor the potato psyllid with yellow traps; silver mulch reduces it during the first 3 to 4 weeks.
Keep the crop free of weeds for the first 12 weeks.
Against powdery mildew, avoid excess nitrogen and direct sprays to the underside of the leaves.
fichas.nota: Table 30: total cost (94,250.60) matches the sum of the items and gross income (225,000) matches 3 t × 75,000 $/t (dried chili). Net income calculated (not printed); the printed B/C of 2.38 is truncated (2.39). The variety and density table (Table 29) came out jumbled; the assignment of each density to each group of chilies was deduced from the order of the text and should be checked against the PDF. The sheet covers chilies for drying; ancho is also harvested green (green chili was not assigned).

fichas.region: Temperate and arid or semiarid subtropical climate, from 200 to 2,700 m a.s.l., with 400 to 600 chill units from November to February. Grows well between 10 and 30 °C and tolerates frosts down to -12 °C. Loam soils, deep (more than 0.5 m) and well drained; more than 400 mm of rain or supplemental irrigation.

siembra.texto: Under irrigation, planting starts in February; under rainfed conditions, during the rains and with potted plants. Use vigorous, uniform nursery plants, bare-root or potted.

fichas.densidad: Spacings of 5 x 5, 4.5 x 4.5, 4 x 4, 3 x 4 and 4 x 2 m (up to 1,250 trees/ha), depending on cultivar and rootstock (peach, Nemaguard and Lovell, Adesoto 101, Cadaman or GF 677).
fichas.fertilizacion: First two years: 30-30-30. Irrigated orchards producing 20 t/ha: 90-90-90, or replace according to target yield. Rainfed or low potential: 30-30-30, applied during the rains or in tree basins with supplemental irrigation. Producing trees: 30 % of the dose after harvest. Rely on leaf analysis.
fichas.riego: Five to seven irrigations a year: one of 10 cm before flowering, two of 15 cm every 20 to 25 days until it rains, and three or four light ones (10 cm) after harvest. Localized irrigation lowers consumption to about 5,000 m³/ha per year versus 12,000 by gravity.
fichas.malezas: The critical stage is the rainy season. Mow with a brush cutter without leaving the soil bare to reduce erosion.
fichas.cosecha: When the yellow ground color covers the green and soluble solids exceed 12 °Brix. Harvest early, never after rain, by hand and without bruising, in suitable containers (not plastic buckets or wooden crates). Cool the fruit quickly to 4 °C; it keeps for 2 to 6 weeks at 0-1 °C and 95 % humidity. Under irrigation yield ranges from 3 to 20 t/ha and under rainfed conditions from 0.8 to 3 t/ha; the landrace can reach 20-26 t/ha.
cuidados: On fields with more than 1 % slope, lay out the orchard on contour lines, especially under rainfed conditions.
Prune to an open-vase shape (3 to 4 scaffolds) or Y-shape for high density; at fruiting, keep mixed branches longer than 20 cm and remove water sprouts, bouquet shoots and dead branches.
Thin 30-35 days after flowering, leaving 3 to 4 buds between fruits and removing double fruits.
Apply 30 % of the fertilizer after harvest in producing trees.
Prefer localized irrigation and adjust irrigation to the variety and crop stage.
Manage diseases preventively: winter treatments against peach leaf curl and shot hole, and from flowering against Monilinia.
fichas.nota: The sheet covers irrigated and rainfed (fertilization and planting for both), hence modality null; the cost is for a drip-irrigated orchard. Tables 35 and 36 are embedded in the harvest text (the extractor did not separate them into 'costos'). The year-three cost was taken, the closest to production (37,054.60, matches its items); year one 77,194.63 and year two 27,154.63. The table gives 12.92 t/ha at 12,399.23 $/t (gross income 160,198.05) and a B/C of 1.13, but that B/C is one year of income divided by the accumulated three-year cost (141,403.89); therefore net income and B/C are null. The cultivar table (Table 34) came out split between varieties and planting and keeps only one density (1,250); the other trees/ha figures were lost.

fichas.region: Temperate arid and warm semiarid subtropics, SS cycle, up to 2,400 m a.s.l., with 15 to 27 °C mean from April to July. Nearly flat fields (less than 1 %), soils deeper than 0.5 m, with good drainage and low salt (it is very sensitive to salinity).

siembra.texto: Irrigated: March 25 to April 25 (Flor de Junio León, Flor de Junio Dalia, Flor de Mayo, Pinto San Rafael, Pinto Rarámuri). Limited irrigation: May 15 to June 15 or June 1 to 15, depending on the variety. Rainfed: from the onset of the rains until July 15 or 25, depending on the variety.

fichas.densidad: Precision or semi-precision planter in 76 cm furrows with 10 cm between plants (about 131 thousand plants/ha).
fichas.fertilizacion: Irrigated: 50-60-30, preferably split between the first and second cultivation. Rainfed: 30-50-00 in high and medium potential and 20-30-00 in low potential, all at planting.
fichas.riego: Pre-planting irrigation; first irrigation 30 days after planting, second at the start of flowering, third at the start of pod filling and fourth during grain filling. Under limited irrigation, ensure water at flowering and grain filling, which are the critical stages.
enfermedades: Root rots (Fusarium spp. and Rhizoctonia spp.)
fichas.malezas: Two cultivator passes: the first 25 to 35 days after planting and the second 25 to 30 days later.
fichas.cosecha: When 50 % of the leaves are lemon yellow and the first pods are almost dry. Keep seed from the healthiest, cleanest lot of uniform size, in a cool, dry, ventilated place. Expected yield of 2.6 to 3.5 t/ha under irrigation; under rainfed conditions, 1,000 to 1,500, 700 to 1,000 and 400 to 700 kg/ha in high, medium and low potential areas.
cuidados: Choose the variety according to available water and plant on its date; under rainfed conditions, not after July 15 or 25.
Plow and harrow right after the previous harvest to make use of moisture; level if irrigating by gravity.
Mexican bean beetle: act at one egg mass per six plants or 2 to 3 larval groups per meter of furrow, only in damaged patches; late plantings are at higher risk.
White grub: sample the soil and act at 3 to 4 larvae per 30 x 30 x 30 cm sample; use traps for adults from May to July.
Against root rots: rotate with cereals for at least 3 years, reduce compaction, raise organic matter, avoid heavy irrigations and do not plant too deep.
Ensure water at flowering and grain filling.
fichas.nota: Tables 41 (irrigated) and 42 (rainfed). Total costs match the sum of the items and gross incomes match yield × price ($/t). Net income calculated (not printed); the irrigated B/C is truncated (1.83). The variety tables (Tables 39 and 40) came out inside the irrigation section and without seeding rates in kg/ha. The density text says '131 (plantas ha⁻¹'; with 76 cm × 10 cm that gives about 131 thousand plants/ha.

fichas.region: Temperate arid and warm semiarid subtropics, SS cycle, up to 2,500 m a.s.l. and slope under 4 %. Under rainfed conditions, potential depends on the July-to-September precipitation/evaporation index and on soil depth.

siembra.texto: Irrigated: intermediate cycle from April 20 to May 24 and early cycle from May 15 to June 15. Rainfed: in high potential before June 30; in medium, from the onset of the rains until July 15.

fichas.densidad: Irrigated: 80,000 to 85,000 plants/ha in 76 cm furrows with 15 to 16 cm between plants. Rainfed: 40,000 to 65,000 plants/ha in high potential and 40,000 to 45,000 in medium (76 cm between furrows and 33 cm between plants, 14 to 16 kg/ha of certified seed).
fichas.fertilizacion: High potential: 80-40-00 or 100-40-00, with half of the N and all of the P at planting and the rest of the N at cultivation. Medium potential: 40-40-00 or 60-40-00, all at planting. In acid soils of high potential, apply lime according to soil analysis.
fichas.riego: Ensure water at heading, flowering and grain filling. By gravity: 5 to 7 supplemental irrigations of 10 cm with intermediate hybrids (high potential) and 4 to 6 with early ones (medium). With drip tape: dry planting at 4 cm, one drip tape per furrow with emitters facing up, daily irrigations of 45 to 60 minutes at establishment and then 2 up to 8 hours daily at flowering and grain filling.
fichas.malezas: One cultivation three weeks after emergence and another fifteen days later.
fichas.cosecha: Maturity is reached when the lower leaves turn yellow, the ear husks are dry, the grain breaks when bitten and shows a black spot at the base. Shocking or bundling the stalks helps against cold. Rainfed yield of 2.5 to 6.0 t/ha in high potential and 1.5 to 2.5 t/ha in medium, depending on rainfall.
cuidados: Plant the right material on its date; under high-potential rainfed conditions, before June 30.
White grub and wireworm: sample before planting and act at 3 to 4 larvae per 30 x 30 x 30 cm sample; light traps for adults in May and June.
Fall armyworm: act at 25 % of plants with larvae, on small larvae; monitor with pheromone traps and direct sprays to the underside of the leaves.
As a biological alternative, tepache traps for adults and Bt, fungi or viruses against first- and second-instar larvae.
Make small basins (pileteo) at cultivation in medium and low potential areas to capture rain.
Under irrigation, do not let water run short at heading, flowering and grain filling.
fichas.nota: Tables 47 (irrigated) and 48 (rainfed). Total costs match the sum of the items and gross incomes match yield × price ($/t). Net income calculated (not printed). In the planting section the irrigated and rainfed labels are crossed (under 'Irrigation regime' it talks about rainfed); densities were taken from Tables 45 and 46. The fertilization in the text is for rainfed; the irrigated cost table uses 200-80-00. The H- and VS- hybrids were placed under varieties because they are INIFAP's public material nomenclature; the agenda does not give the company for the commercial ones. The irrigated yield appears only in the cost table (12 t/ha).

fichas.region: Temperate arid and warm semiarid subtropics, up to 2,500 m a.s.l. and slope under 4 %. Under rainfed conditions, yield depends on the July-to-September rainfall balance and on soil depth.

siembra.texto: Irrigated: intermediate cycle from April 20 to May 24 and early cycle from June 1 to July 15. Rainfed: high potential before July 10; medium to low, from the onset of the rains until July 15.

fichas.densidad: Irrigated (Table 51): 90,000 to 95,000 plants/ha with intermediate materials and 80,000 to 85,000 with early ones. Rainfed: 40,000 to 65,000 plants/ha in high potential and 40,000 to 45,000 in medium to low. Furrows of 76 cm.
fichas.fertilizacion: High potential: 80-40-00, with all of the P and half of the N at planting and the rest of the N at cultivation; lime acid soils according to analysis. Medium potential: 40-40-00 or 60-40-00, all at planting.
fichas.malezas: One cultivation three weeks after emergence and another fifteen days later.
fichas.cosecha: For silage, chop at 30 to 35 % dry matter (it can be measured by drying 150 g in an air fryer at 121 °C for 30 minutes). For bundling, cut with the upper half still green, dry in the field, bundle and grind at about 12 % moisture; store in the shade. The text gives 35 to 45 t/ha of fresh forage (12 to 16 t/ha dry) and 80 to 90 t/ha (24 to 32 t/ha dry) in high potential depending on the regime (see note).
cuidados: Choose the material according to regime and potential and plant on its date (rainfed: before July 10 or 15).
Measure dry matter before chopping for silage (30 to 35 %).
Sample white grub and wireworm before planting (3 to 4 larvae per 30 x 30 x 30 cm sample).
Fall armyworm and armyworm: act at 25 % of plants with larvae, on small larvae, supported by pheromone traps; alternatives: tepache traps, Bt, fungi and viruses.
Make small basins (pileteo) at cultivation in medium and low potential areas.
Prefer vertical tillage to conserve moisture under rainfed conditions.
fichas.nota: Tables 53 (irrigated) and 54 (rainfed), in t of green forage and $/t. Total costs match the sum of the items and gross incomes match yield × price. Net income calculated (not printed); the printed B/C values are truncated (1.86 and 1.99). In the planting section the irrigated and rainfed labels seem crossed (under irrigation it gives 40,000-65,000 plants/ha and under rainfed 90,000-95,000, the opposite of the variety tables); density was taken from the tables. The yield text also seems crossed (rainfed 80-90 t/ha and irrigated 35-45 t/ha, versus 90 and 40 t/ha in the cost tables). Table 52 (rainfed) came out inside the planting section.

fichas.region: Temperate arid and semiarid zones, from 300 to 2,200 m a.s.l. and 18 to 22 °C mean; with 400 mm of rain a year, harvests of 10 t/ha are assured. It is damaged by frequent frosts below -8 °C. Loam soils deeper than 50 cm; on slopes over 2 %, lay out contour lines.

siembra.texto: Cladodes are cut at pruning (December to February), left to dehydrate for about 15 days and planted from April to June, burying half and with the faces oriented east to west. If it does not rain, irrigate at 30 or 40 days, or plant 20 to 40 days before the rains.

fichas.densidad: Spacings of 5 x 5, 4.5 x 4.5, 5 x 4, 4 x 4, 5 x 3, 4 x 3.5 and 4 x 3 m depending on the cultivar; the cost table uses 667 plants/ha.
fichas.fertilizacion: Year 1: 8 kg of manure + 150 g of ammonium sulfate per plant. Year 2: 150 g of ammonium sulfate + 150 g of superphosphate + 100 g of potassium chloride. Year 3: 16 kg of manure + 200 g of ammonium sulfate + 150 g of superphosphate + 100 g of potassium chloride. From year 4, manure in alternate years and the year-3 fertilization. Rainfed: 45-15-15 at the start of the rains. Irrigated: 90-30-30, with half of the N and all of the P and K at the first irrigation before sprouting and the rest of the N after harvest.
fichas.riego: Supplemental drip irrigation: one a week before sprouting (9 hours) and another 40 days later (6 hours), with 4 emitters of 4 L/h per plant; it saves up to 56 % of the water. It is stopped when the rains begin.
fichas.malezas: Control annual weeds especially in the rainy season and watch perennial ones almost all year. Between plants, by hand or with a brush cutter; between rows, mow or cut without leaving the soil bare.
fichas.cosecha: For export, harvest at the color change ('rayada'); for consumption, at full maturity. Harvest early when humidity is high to reduce the spines, wearing goggles, gloves and protective clothing; cut with a knife without twisting or bruising the fruit and use crates of 25 kg maximum. Under rainfed conditions 3 to 9 t/ha are obtained and under irrigation 4.4 to 20 t/ha; Cristalina and Rojo Liso can reach 33.5 and 32.6 t/ha.
cuidados: Plant healthy cladodes 2 years old or older from April to June, dehydrated for about 15 days and with the cuts protected.
Give open-vase training pruning during the first three years (February-March) and sanitary pruning throughout the cycle, disinfecting tools with chlorine and water 1:1.
Remove and burn plants with chatilla as soon as they are detected and use healthy mother plants in new orchards.
Manage pests with monitoring according to the crop stage and the cycle of each insect.
Apply at least 30 % of the nitrogen one month after harvest.
Thin flower buds 1 to 2 weeks before flowering to improve fruit size.
fichas.nota: The sheet covers irrigated and rainfed (fertilization, yields and supplemental irrigation), hence modality null. Costs from Table 59 (producing orchard, no irrigation expenses): cost 23,940 matches its items and gross income 28,500 matches 9,500 kg × 3 $/kg; B/C of 1.19 is consistent; net income calculated. Table 60 (years two and three, with irrigation) gives 15,786.80 and 25,607.14 $/ha (they match), but its 'total cost' of 63,336.94 does not correspond to any clear sum; with 20.24 t/ha at 4,657.66 $/t it gives gross income of 94,271.04 and a B/C of 1.48 on that accumulated total. The cultivar table (Table 58) came out split between varieties and density and lost the trees/ha. Rojo Liso was taken from the diseases and harvest text.

fichas.region: Best from 0 to 1,600 m a.s.l. (medium up to 1,800), 15 to 25 °C mean and more than 450 mm of rain from the third ten-day period of June to the first of October (350 to 450 mm for medium potential). Slope under 4 % and soil deeper than 0.5 m.

siembra.texto: From the onset of the rains until July 31.

fichas.densidad: 18 to 20 kg/ha of seed for 20 to 25 plants per linear meter, in 76 cm furrows with double rows 20 cm apart.
fichas.fertilizacion: 80-60-00 in high potential, 60-40-00 in medium and 40-30-00 in low, before or at planting. A prior soil analysis is advisable.
fichas.malezas: Plant into moist soil after harrowing to eliminate weeds; two cultivations, the first with the sorghum at 10 to 15 cm and the second at 20 to 25 cm. Broadleaf weeds are the most common. Make small basins (pileteo) at cultivation.
fichas.cosecha: At the milk stage of the grain, 115 days after planting (soft grain that releases a milky liquid with a fingernail). By hand, make bundles and grind when the forage is dehydrated. Expected yield of 18 t/ha of green matter in high potential and 10 t/ha in medium.
cuidados: Plant with the first rains and no later than July 31.
Use the recommended varieties: they resist lodging, birds damage them little and they tolerate diseases.
Make small basins (pileteo) and plant on contour lines to capture rainwater; in medium potential and late plantings, from planting and in all furrows.
Fall armyworm: act at more than 10 % of plants with small larvae (20 % of damaged plants in the case of Pseudaletia).
Against aphids, biodegradable detergent (4 g/L) or lacewing release after sampling.
Harvest at the milk stage, at around 115 days.
fichas.nota: Table 63: total cost (13,432.70) matches the sum of the items and gross income (13,483.80) matches 18 t of green matter × 749.10 $/t; B/C of 1.00 is consistent; net income calculated. The agenda calls Pseudaletia unipuncta 'fall armyworm' (which in the maize sheets is the armyworm) and mentions aphids only in the control alternatives. It does not give the origin of the varieties; all were left under varieties. June was included in the months because the rain window in the table starts in the third ten-day period of June. The sheet has no separate region section: the requirements came inside the introduction.

fichas.region: Temperate arid and warm semiarid subtropics, up to 2,500 m a.s.l. Best with 0 to 1 % slope, medium texture, soil deeper than 0.5 m and electrical conductivity below 4 mmhos/cm.

siembra.texto: Irrigated (FW): December 15 to January 20. Rainfed (SS): from the onset of the rains until July 30.

fichas.densidad: Irrigated: 75 kg/ha of seed in double-row furrows and 120 kg/ha broadcast or in corrugations. Rainfed: 80 kg/ha in double rows with small basins (pileteo) and 130 kg/ha in corrugations with small basins or broadcast. Furrows of 76 cm with rows 20 cm apart; seed no deeper than 5 cm.
fichas.fertilizacion: Irrigated: 120-60-00, with 60-60-00 at planting and 60-00-00 at tillering (broadcast or in corrugations, before tillering). In sandy soils, split the N; in clay soils, apply everything at planting. Rainfed: 40-40-00 in high potential, 30-30-00 in medium and 20-20-00 in low, at planting.
fichas.riego: With severe water restriction: planting irrigation and irrigations at 45 and 75 days. With moderate availability: 45, 75 and 100 days. Without restriction: up to five irrigations at 15, 35, 65, 85 and 105 days. Drip tape allows fertilizer to be applied through irrigation.
fichas.malezas: Plant into moist soil and harrow before planting. Broadleaf weeds are controlled at tillering; watch for wild oats between 25 and 30 days after planting.
fichas.cosecha: At physiological maturity: golden head and hard grain that does not split with a fingernail. By hand, bundles and threshing at 12 % moisture. Under irrigation, up to 6 t/ha in high potential and 4 t/ha in medium; under rainfed conditions, 2.5 to 3.0 t/ha in high and 2.0 to 2.5 t/ha in medium.
cuidados: Plant on time: December 15 to January 20 under irrigation and before July 30 under rainfed conditions.
Use the recommended varieties, which are tolerant to diseases.
Watch for aphids in the early stages, especially Russian wheat aphid and greenbug: management is justified at 4 aphids per seedling or 10 per tiller.
As an alternative, biodegradable detergent (4 g/L) or release lacewings (1 egg per 2 aphids).
Make small basins (pileteo) under rainfed conditions: in high potential at the boot stage, and in medium potential or late plantings from planting and in all furrows.
Level the field to distribute irrigation water well.
fichas.nota: Tables 67 (irrigated) and 68 (rainfed). Irrigated: total cost matches its items and gross income (24,182.09) matches 3.74 t × 6,465.80 $/t. Rainfed: the planting line says 720 but its items add up to 1,920, and the printed total cost (10,172.42) matches neither sum (9,572.42 or 10,772.42); the printed one was kept because it is consistent with gross income (11,650) and the B/C (1.15). Net incomes calculated (not printed). Nana F2007 appears only in the cost table.

fichas.region: Temperate arid subtropical climate; vineyards in Ojocaliente, Villa Hidalgo and Fresnillo. Well-drained soils deeper than 50 cm, medium or coarse texture and 0 to 4 % slope. There are two zones by accumulated heat: Region I (cool) and Region II (moderately warm).

siembra.texto: Plant at the end of winter, between February and March, with rooted or grafted plants (one individual per vine), or with two callused canes per vine, keeping the more vigorous one.

variedades: Red wine grapes: Aleático, Barbera, Cabernet Franc, Cabernet Sauvignon, Carignan, Gamay, Grenache, Malbec, Merlot, Nebbiolo, Petite Syrah, Pinot Noir, Sangiovese, Shiraz, Souzao, Valdepeñas, Zinfandel
White wine grapes: Blanche, Chasselas Doré, Chardonnay, Chenin Blanc, Clairette Blanche, Gewürztraminer, Melón, Red Veltliner, Sauvignon Blanc, Semillón, Sylvaner, White Riesling
White table grapes: Calmeria, Dattier de Beyrouth, Italia, Muscat, Olivette Blanche, Servant
Red table grapes: Emperador, Flame Tokay, Flame, Kishmishi, Málaga Roja, Queen, Red Globe, Ruby Seedless
Black table grapes: Black Rose, Exotic, Moscatel de Hamburgo, Ribier
fichas.densidad: Low-vigor wine varieties (Merlot, Cabernet Franc, Riesling, Gewürztraminer): 3,333 (2 x 1.50 m) to 4,000 plants/ha (2 x 1.25 m). Vigorous ones (Cabernet Sauvignon, Malbec, Valdepeñas, Semillón, Chardonnay): 2,222 (3 x 1.50 m) to 2,666 plants/ha (3 x 1.25 m). Table grapes: 1,851 plants/ha.
fichas.fertilizacion: First year: 30-30-30 before planting. Years 2 and 3, with irrigation: 80-30-80. In production (4 years or more): 120-35-120, with 70 % of the N and all of the P and K from budbreak to veraison and the rest of the N after harvest. Adjust with soil and petiole analysis.
fichas.riego: New vineyard: planting irrigation (48 mm) and then 16 mm per week until the rains. In production: every 20 to 25 days from budbreak to harvest; after leaf fall, keep light moisture. It requires at least 572 mm of water from March to September in addition to rainfall.
plagas: Yellow spider mite or Lewis mite (Eotetranychus lewisi)
fichas.malezas: Run a brush cutter, manual or rotary, between rows and between plants.
fichas.cosecha: Table grapes by appearance, size and sugars (14 to 18 °Brix); wine grapes at 20.5 to 23 °Brix and pH below 3.3. Mechanical harvest is cheaper but risks wine quality. Cool quickly; grapes keep 4 to 6 weeks at 0.5-2.5 °C and 90-95 % humidity. Low-vigor wine varieties give 10 to 15 t/ha and vigorous table varieties up to 30 t/ha; with good technification, an average of 20 t/ha. The break-even point is estimated in the seventh year at 12.42 t/ha.
cuidados: Use phylloxera-resistant rootstocks (Rupestris du Lot, 110 Richter, 99 Richter, SO4): the pest has affected 65 % of the table-grape vineyards of Ojocaliente.
Choose varieties according to use (table or wine) and the region by accumulated heat.
Adjust density and training system to the vigor of the variety.
Prune according to vigor (short, long or mixed) and in summer remove poorly placed shoots and leaves at cluster level.
Irrigate every 20 to 25 days from budbreak to harvest and rely on petiole analysis to fertilize.
Consider the high initial investment: the break-even point arrives around the seventh year.
fichas.nota: Tables 75 and 76 are embedded in the harvest text (the extractor did not separate them into 'costos'). Year one: 375,125 $/ha (matches its items). Year two: the table prints 27,154.63, but its items add up to 27,100.54 (the printed figure is the same as for peach). Year three: it prints 43,747.40 and its items add up to 43,797.40. For that reason the production cost is null. The table gives 20 t/ha at 10,264.48 $/t (gross income 205,289.60) and a B/C of 0.46 calculated against the accumulated three-year cost (446,026.66); net income and B/C are null. The varieties were grouped by use and color, combining those of Regions I and II (Tables 73 and 74).
